title: Session-harmonized fanout controller for atomic A/B promotions
author: Maya Thompson
description: Motivation: A/B promotions and staged swaps can split a user's session across variants during short transitory windows leading to inconsistent UX and hard-to-interpret telemetry. This PR adds a 'session-harmonized fanout controller' (SHF) to ensure atomic visibility of promotional swaps per session while preserving safe rollback semantics. Goals: 1) guarantee session-affine traffic assignment for the duration of an atomic promote/commit operation; 2) maintain low latency for steady-state traffic; 3) provide deterministic, replayable rollback paths; 4) integrate with existing rollout guard rails and telemetry gates. Summary of changes: implemented a controller that groups incoming requests by session-hash and forwards them to the active variant for that session; when a promotion window is opened the controller pins session groups to candidate variant atomically via a lightweight transaction and a per-transaction drain cohort; added a new 'rollout_transactions' control-plane resource to track in-flight promos, their TTLs, and snapshot checkpoints for fast revert; extended the routing runtime to consult an in-memory session-map with two-level caching (hot-session LRU + prefix-shared KV) to keep p99 token-matching overhead minimal; added CLI and Console UI for viewing active transactions and manual aborts; added e2e smoke and determinism tests and microbenchmarks. Implementation notes: control-plane: api/rollouts.proto adds RolloutTransaction RPCs and hooks for snapshot and rewind; database: new schema migration to create rollout_transactions table (id:uuid, transaction_state, pinned_sessions:text[], snapshot_version, created_at, expires_at); runtime: internal/orchestrator/fanout_controller.go implements transaction lifecycle (prepare->pin->drain->commit/abort) with backpressure smoothing to avoid surge when commit flips large cohorts; routing: runtime/cache/session_map.go supports session affinity with fallback to hashed bucketing; observability: added metrics rollout.transaction.duration_ms, rollout.transaction.pinned_sessions and traces for transaction lifecycle. Tests & CI: unit tests cover transaction state transitions; e2e session deterministic test replays 10k session traces to validate no cross-variant leaks; microbenchmarks show median per-request latency +0.9ms at 95th percentile under synthetic skewed session workloads, worst-case +3ms while prepare/commit flows are active; added an experiment harness to load test at scale and measure rollback success rates. Migration and backward compatibility: the new routing consults session-map only when rollouts have active transactions; default behavior unchanged for customers without active promotions; migration script creates rollout_transactions table and backfills no-op snapshots for existing rollouts. Rollout & failure modes: commit uses a two-phase prepare/commit with a drain window and optional replay buffer to ensure ordered session handoff; abort triggers immediate revert using snapshot_version for deterministic traffic reconciliation; fallback policy implemented to fall back to previous variant if commit fails more than 2 times or if telemetry gates report a delta breach. UX: Console updates include transaction timeline, pinned session count, and a manual abort button with validation. CLI: redwoodctl rollout transaction status | promote | abort. Performance tuning: added batching of commit acknowledgements and sampled tracing to keep overhead reasonable. Related: ENG-3124 (session-consistency for experiments), ENG-3187 (rollback-playback library). Risks: transient latency spikes during commit for heavy session skews; mitigations include configurable drain window and rate-limited commit. TODOs: add adaptive drain sizing (follow-up), integrate with Dedicated autoscaler to reserve commit capacity, surface per-customer default drain presets in Console. Reviewers' requested work that was addressed: - rename transaction->rollout_transaction across API and DB; - add additional e2e case for long-running websocket sessions; - add safety TTL for stale transactions; - include unit tests for abort path. This description is a condensed single-string summary as required.
